title: Visiting every value
idea: Opener: a list holds many values; often you want to do the SAME action to each one, in order. Thinking first, no new syntax yet.

exercises.prompt: You have a basket of apples and you want to polish EVERY apple. What are you doing?
options: The same action to each item, one at a time
One action to the whole basket at once
exercises.explanation: Polishing every apple means repeating the SAME action for each item in turn. That 'do it to each one' idea is this unit's whole job.

exercises.prompt: 'Do something to every value in a list' means repeating the same step for each item, in order.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. You visit item 1, do the step; item 2, do the step; and so on to the end.

exercises.prompt: A list of scores is [10, 7, 9]. You want to print each score on its own line. How many times does the printing step happen?
exercises.explanation: One action per item: three scores means the print step runs three times.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are 'do the same thing to every item' tasks? (pick all)
options: Print each name in a guest list
Add a star after each score
Double every price in a list
exercises.explanation: Printing each, starring each, and doubling each all repeat one action per item. Reading just the first item is a single step, not a per-item action.

exercises.prompt: You want to greet every name in a guest list. Put the plain-English steps in order.
blocks: Take the next name from the list
Stop when the list is finished
exercises.explanation: Take a name, greet it, repeat; stop at the end. That take-one / do-the-step / repeat rhythm is what a loop over a list gives you.

exercises.prompt: When you do something to every value, the computer handles the items one at a time, from first to last.
exercises.explanation: A list keeps its order, so the loop walks it front to back — item 1, then 2, then 3.

exercises.prompt: Last unit you could already loop with range(n). Why might 'go through each item of a list' feel easier for a list?
options: You get each value directly, without using its position number
Lists can't be looped any other way
exercises.explanation: Instead of asking for position 0, 1, 2... you can grab each value itself. That's the comfort this unit's tool gives you.

exercises.prompt: Match each everyday task to what 'visiting every value' would do.

pairs.left: Water each plant on the shelf
Add up a bill at the end
pairs.right: not per-item — a single result (later unit)

exercises.explanation: Marking and watering repeat one action per item. Totalling is a different pattern we meet in a later unit — not yet.

exercises.prompt: A list of temperatures is [18, 21, 16]. You want to print 'Nice' once for each temperature. What will you see?
exercises.explanation: One action per item, three items: 'Nice' appears three times. The action doesn't have to use the value.

exercises.prompt: This unit gives you one new tool. What is it for?
options: Going through a list and doing something with each value
exercises.explanation: Next you'll meet 'for item in list' — the clean way to visit every value and act on it.
